title: Customer Fargate host stays PROVISIONING after RunTask
description:
**Labeled stop from `chatticus-3e72dc16-ff6f-44f2-8d3c-dd3a49f9ac52` browser_open (2026-09-07).** Do not retry the matrix row until a customer host reaches RUNNING and executes `browser_open`.

`chatticus-82dab7c4-a44c-4e0e-ac19-51a0c7a12d09` proved customer-account `RunTask ≥ 1`. It did **not** prove a host that stays up and executes a tool.

## Confirming check (2026-09-07) — IaC hypothesis **falsified**

Hypothesis on this card: Anthus ECR has no resource policy, so the customer task dies on `CannotPullContainerError` (authorization).

**AWS (lab operator, not root; placeholders here):**

- Anthus `ComputerImage` repository policy **already** has `Sid: ChatticusCustomerAccountPull` for the customer account root (`ecr:BatchCheckLayerAvailability`, `BatchGetImage`, `GetDownloadUrlForLayer`). Runtime merge in `anthus_computer_ecr_pull.py` ran. `computer-stack.ts` still has no CDK `addToResourcePolicy`; that part of the IaC read was true and **not** the live failure.
- Original browser_open task is **MISSING** from ECS history.
- 41 stopped tasks: **all** `stopCode=EssentialContainerExited`, `stoppedReason=Essential container in task exited`, container `reason` empty. **Pull succeeded** (~10–20 s `pullStartedAt` → `pullStoppedAt`). **Zero** `CannotPullContainerError`.
- CloudWatch on the customer log group: `computer_host_worker` crashes at `ControlPlane.ensure_computer` → `DynamoMessagingStore.get_computer` → **`AccessDeniedException` `dynamodb:GetItem`**. Principal is the **customer-account** task role `ChatticusComputers-ComputerTaskRole*` assumed in `CUSTOMER_ACCOUNT_ID`. Exit code **1**.
- `infra/lib/computer-host-start.ts` grants Dynamo + computer-turn SQS to the **Anthus** imported host task role. `infra/lib/customer-computers-stack.ts` grants the customer task role **nothing** for Dynamo (and should not, under `chatticus-8a25af4a-7ae7-44e6-8229-e1d8313b712b`).

**Named cause:** `HOST_TASK_ROLE_DYNAMO_ACCESS_DENIED`. The customer Fargate task pulls the image, starts `computer_host_worker`, and the process uses `plane_from_env()` (Dynamo) instead of the Front Door only. Anthus table is not callable from that role. That is why `tool.call` has no `tool.result`.

Do **not** patch this bug by adding `dynamodb:*` to the customer task role. Do **not** patch it as an Anthus ECR policy gap. Image location is a separate principle card; this bug is the host talking to Dynamo from the wrong account.

## Feature: Customer computer host becomes usable

```
Feature: A dispatched customer computer host reaches RUNNING and executes a tool

  Scenario: browser_open completes on the customer host
    Given host start has been dispatched into the customer account
    And the customer task role cannot call Anthus DynamoDB
    When the computer continuation job is on the queue
    Then the customer Fargate task reaches RUNNING
    And computer_host_worker does not AccessDenied on GetItem
    And the turn journal contains tool.result opened:about:blank
```

## Done when

A live kernel `browser_open` / `about:blank` against the customer-account computer yields `opened:about:blank` in the journal, customer `RunTask` (not Anthus), and CloudWatch does not show Dynamo `AccessDenied` on the customer task role. Wiki placeholders. Do not fold elapsed time into ~19 min.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
## Root-cause hypothesis from the IaC (2026-09-07)

Read from the stack definitions, not from AWS — **confirm before acting**. But it predicts exactly the observed symptom: a task that never reaches RUNNING and a `tool.call` with no `tool.result`.

**The customer task pulls its image from the Anthus registry, and the Anthus registry does not allow it.**

- `infra/lib/customer-computers-stack.ts:69` — `image: ecs.ContainerImage.fromRegistry(anthusComputerImageUri.valueAsString)`, with the parameter described at line 30 as *"Anthus ChatticusComputers ECR image URI for tag :dev."*
- `infra/lib/computer-stack.ts` — **no** `addToResourcePolicy`, `grantPull`, or repository policy of any kind. Cross-account ECR pull requires a resource-based policy on the **source** repository granting the puller account `ecr:BatchGetImage` and `ecr:GetDownloadUrlForLayer`. The customer's execution-role permissions (lines 87–90 of the customer stack) are necessary and not sufficient — they authorize the caller, not the repository.

Networking is not the problem: `natGateways: 0` with `SubnetType.PUBLIC` and `assignPublicIp: true` is the standard reachable-Fargate pattern, so ECR is routable.

## This contradicts the recorded plan

`chatticus-82dab7`'s who-creates-what table says:

> Computer image `:dev` in that ECR | **Chatticus under the assumed role** | `PutImage` already allowed; customer does not docker-push

And the published role backs that design — `infra/customer-role.yml` grants the **full push set**: `ecr:CreateRepository`, `PutImage`, `InitiateLayerUpload`, `UploadLayerPart`, `CompleteLayerUpload`, plus `SetRepositoryPolicy`.

**So the role is provisioned to push the image into the customer's own ECR, and the stack is written to pull it from Anthus's.** One of the two is wrong.

## Confirming check

```
aws ecs describe-tasks --cluster <customer cluster> --tasks <task arn> \
  --query 'tasks[].{last:lastStatus,stopped:stoppedReason,c:containers[].reason}'
```

A `CannotPullContainerError` naming authorization confirms this. Anything else falsifies it — record that and this hypothesis is wrong.

## The design question underneath

Which is the intended shape?

- **Image in the customer's ECR** (what the role is built for, and what `82dab7` recorded). Self-contained account, consistent with "their account", no dependency on Anthus registry availability or a cross-account policy at task-start time. Costs a push per customer per image version.
- **Pull from Anthus's registry** (what the stack does). One copy to maintain, but every customer task start depends on an Anthus-side resource policy, and Anthus can change the image under a customer without them re-running anything.

Worth settling deliberately rather than by whichever gets patched first. It is the same axis as the snapshot-bucket decision (`chatticus-bb9084`) and the dict-vs-host-disk decision (`chatticus-fccc4e`): **how self-contained is the customer's account actually meant to be?** Three separate cards are now answering that question one resource at a time.

comments.text:
Confirming check done (lab operator, not root). **IaC hypothesis falsified.**

Anthus `ComputerImage` already has `ChatticusCustomerAccountPull` for the customer account. 41 stopped tasks: all `EssentialContainerExited` after a successful pull (~10–20 s). Zero `CannotPullContainerError`. CloudWatch: customer task role `AccessDenied` on Anthus Dynamo `GetItem` from `computer_host_worker` / `plane_from_env()`. Named cause `HOST_TASK_ROLE_DYNAMO_ACCESS_DENIED`.

Do not grant the customer task role Dynamo. Do not treat this as an ECR policy gap. Image self-containment is `chatticus-2b3c4173-a431-45fb-aec0-c6f4aa921b51` (waits on this host actually running).

Composer 2.5 planning: worktree `/tmp/chatticus-8fe4c7-host-http` on `fix/8fe4c7-host-front-door`. Implementation not authorized until the plan is reviewed.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
Plan **not authorized**. Worktree `/tmp/chatticus-8fe4c7-host-http` was named and does not exist. Shared-queue SQS consume from the customer task role is rejected.

ComputerTurnJobs is one Anthus queue for the environment. Customer `ReceiveMessage` on it can steal other tenants' jobs. `waiting_computer_job` via the Front Door is the job path for this slice. Lambda ComputerWorker keeps SQS. If that is not enough, Front Door receives SQS with Anthus creds — never the customer role on the shared queue.

Do not add a customer-visible SQS policy in this slice. Do not mint a dozen computer routes before listing the ControlPlane methods `ComputerHostBootDriver` and `ComputerWorker.run_job` actually call. `POST /computers/stopped` is a user route today; the host is a worker.
